reason: Creation narrative of God making the animals; not a direction. Shares only 'according to their kind' wording with Noah's ark instruction.
God's sworn promise of blessing after the test; a promise directing no one. It recalls Abraham's obedience, not the command in 22:12.
Promise of blessing through Abraham's seed; directs no one. The similar 26:4 is promise inside Isaac's record, not its direction.
Dialogue lead-in ('Father' / 'Who are you?'); no direction. Jacob's request is recorded at 27:19; Genesis 22:7 shares only the address.
Isaac's blessing-wish ('may my God bless you'); a blessing directing no one. His charge is recorded at 28:1–2 with 28:6 linked.
Fulfilment narrative: Jacob builds the altar commanded in 35:1; it echoes the wording but does not quote or cite the command.
Reuben's lament over Joseph's absence; narrative speech with no direction. Shares only the word 'child' with Luke 15:31.
Joseph's interpretation predicting famine; a prediction directing no one. His advice to Pharaoh, from 41:33, is already recorded.
Judah continues the same recollection of Joseph's demand that Benjamin come down; same speaker and occasion as 44:21; wording matches 43:3–5.

context: Judah quotes to Joseph Jacob's warning that losing Benjamin would bring his old age down to Hades in sorrow.
reason: Judah reports Jacob's refusal to risk Benjamin, repeating the warning of 42:38 almost verbatim; another speaker and occasion, so parallel.

context: Judah tells Joseph of the surety he pledged to Jacob for Benjamin, quoting 43:9.
reason: Judah quotes the surety of 43:9 ('If I do not bring him to you'), which the record holds as part of the request.
Fulfilment narrative of Jacob's burial charge (49:29–32); repeats the cave description but does not quote or cite the charge.
Genealogy of Kohath's sons; narrative list with no direction. Numbers 3:19 is a genealogy verse inside a broad range record.
Moses' assurance (prediction) that the frogs will be removed; directs no one. Pharaoh's request is recorded at 8:4.

context: Narrator reports Israel asking the Egyptians as Moses instructed, repeating 11:3's note of the favour the Lord gave.
reason: 12:35 expressly cites Moses' instruction; 12:36 repeats 11:3 verbatim and completes the report. Reference widened to include unattached 12:35.
Narrative of the calf feast; Paul quotes it as an example in 1 Corinthians 10:7, but the verse itself directs no one.
Fulfilment narrative: the third day's leader presents his gift as ordered in 7:11; no citation of the direction.
Fulfilment narrative: the eleventh day's leader presents his gift; shares only the leader's name with the census list at 1:13.
Narrative of the first march from Sinai (10:11–28); 'shall set out' follows the Greek tense; plain fulfilment of the 2:31 order.
Moses' complaint addressed to God (prayer, 11:11–15); not a direction. Shares wording with Jethro's advice in Exodus 18:18 only.
Census genealogy naming Zelophehad's daughters; no direction. Joshua 17:3–6 is linked because the daughters cite the ruling there; this verse cites nothing.
Census genealogy of Levi's clans; narrative list, not a direction.
Narrative note on Nadab and Abihu's death within the census; not a direction.
Narrative summary of the census done by Moses and Eleazar; plain fulfilment of 26:1–4 with no direction stated.
Narrator recalls the Lord's sentence of death in the wilderness and notes its fulfilment; a judgment, not a direction.
Moses recalls God's oath excluding the exodus generation except Caleb and Joshua; a judgment within his rebuke, not a direction.
God's promise of Israel's borders, recalling the promise of Deuteronomy 11:24; directs no one. The commission is recorded at 1:2 and 1:6–9.
Joshua's assurance of conquest ('by this you shall know'); a promise, not a direction. His call to hear (3:9) is recorded.

context: Narrator reports the eastern tribes crossing equipped before Israel, just as Moses had commanded them.
reason: Fulfilment expressly citing the command ('just as Moses had commanded them'); matches Deuteronomy 3:18, 'Go armed before your brethren, the sons of Israel'.
Joshua formally appoints the Gibeonites woodcutters and water-carriers that day: the assignment of 9:21–23, same speaker and occasion.
List of defeated kings; narrative, not a direction. Shares only place names with Jabin's coalition summons.

context: Narrator reports Israel dividing the land as the Lord had commanded Moses.
reason: Fulfilment expressly citing the Lord's command to Moses on dividing the land; same target as the pending link of Joshua 14:2.
Boundary description in Zebulun's allotment; narrative geography, not a direction. Shares wording with Numbers 34:5 only.
Boundary description in Asher's allotment; narrative geography, not a direction. Shares wording with Numbers 34:5 only.
Narrative introduction to Joshua's speech; his dismissal and charge are recorded at 22:4 and 22:5. The verse itself states no direction.
The rulers' deliberation and conditional offer among themselves; directs no one. The elders' actual commission of Jephthah is recorded (11:6, 11:8–11).
Rhetorical question within Jephthah's message (the sending is AUD-07-11-12); not a direction. Shares only Balak's name with Numbers 22:10.
The people renew the 8:5 demand for a king at the same assembly (8:4–22), so extend; 8:19 begins the sentence.
Saul's oath that David shall not die; a sworn undertaking about his own action, not a direction to anyone.
David's protest of innocence; 'know and see' is an appeal, not a direction. His restraint toward Saul is already linked at 24:5–8.
David's appeal for the Lord to judge between them; a prayer-wish, not a direction. Shares wording with Proverbs 22:23 only.
Narrative of Abner and Ish-bosheth's servants moving to Gibeon; not a direction.
List of David's officials; narrative, not a direction. Shares only the priests' names with 15:35.
Bathsheba carries out Nathan's recorded advice (fulfilment); the oath she recalls is a promise. Her petition 1:17–21 is item N:GAP-11-1-17.
Narrative of Solomon's God-given wisdom; not a direction. Matches 2:35a only because AUD-11-2-35's '1 Kings 2:35' sweeps in the Greek supplements.
Narrative of Solomon's labour force; not a direction. Matches 2:35d only because AUD-11-2-35's reference sweeps in the Greek supplements 2:35a–o.
Narrative description of Solomon's overseers; not a direction. Matches 2:35h only through AUD-11-2-35's sweep of the Greek supplements.
Narrative of the extent of Solomon's rule; not a direction. Matches 2:46k only because AUD-11-2-46's '1 Kings 2:46' sweeps in the Greek supplements.
Narrative of Jeroboam's flight to Egypt; not a direction. Matches 12:24c only because ot-1-kings-v12-23's range sweeps in the Greek supplement.
Elijah's judgment oracle on Ahab's house; a prediction directing no one. 2 Kings 9:9 repeats it inside Jehu's commission, whose direction is 9:7.
Jehoshaphat's request for a prophet of the Lord opens the recorded exchange; its Chronicles parallel 18:6 is already linked to this record.
Elijah delivers the oracle in person: rebuke and death sentence, directing no one. 1:6 is recorded for the messengers' charge to return and tell.
Hezekiah sends the delegation that carries the recorded message (19:3–4); the parallel Isaiah 37:2–4 record likewise includes the sending.

context: Chronicles account of the elders' covenant with David at Hebron and his anointing, according to the Lord's word through Samuel.
reason: Chronicles parallel of the same Hebron covenant and anointing; 1 Chronicles 11:2 is already linked to AUD-10-5-2 in the same way.

context: Nathan's oracle first designates David's offspring as builder of God's house, the designation recalled in 22:10 and 28:6.
reason: Original divine designation of the temple builder; its near-verbatim recollections 22:10 and 28:6 are already linked to this record.

context: Chronicles account of David sending Joab and the whole army of mighty men against Ammon.
reason: Chronicles parallel of the same sending of Joab and the army against Ammon, recorded at 2 Samuel 10:7.
Hiram's reply describing the artisan he supplied: fulfilment of Solomon's 2:6 request, with no direction. Hiram's sending (2:12) is item N:GAP-14-2-12.

context: Chronicles account of Rehoboam consulting Solomon's elders and their counsel to show the people favour and speak good words.
reason: Chronicles parallel of the elders' counsel; reference adds 10:6, the consultation matching 1 Kings 12:6 in the record's own Scripture.
Narrative of the people destroying Baal's house; not a direction. 2 Kings 11:18 is linked only for Jehoiada's appointment, held at 23:18.
Chronicles narrates the silver reaching the workers with no order stated; plain fulfilment of 2 Kings 22:5 (R5b separately proposes linking 34:10–12).
The letter's opening blessing-wish ('May God do good to you'); a prayer, not a direction. The letter's direction is recorded at 1:9.
Nehemiah's further order in the same fire-recovery procedure, with the same liquid as 1:21; extend rather than a new record (cf. N:GAP-16-1-31).
Closing greeting and date of the Roman envoys' letter; no direction. That letter (11:34–38) is item N:GAP-16-11-34.

context: Nehemiah's copy of the returnees' register repeats the governor's ruling barring unproven priests from the most holy things.
reason: The Nehemiah list repeats the governor's ruling recorded at Ezra 2:63, nearly word for word.
The king's question soliciting counsel; not itself a direction. Haman's proposals (6:8–9) and the king's order (6:10) are recorded.
Job's maxim within his argument; in 34:3 the same image is Elihu's reason, not the direction. Shared proverb, no direction here.
Eliphaz's description of Job's calamities; accusation, not a direction. Shares only light and darkness wording with Luke 11:35.
Elihu's claim that God's spirit made and teaches him; doctrine about himself. His calls to hear and answer are recorded at 33:1 and 33:5.
Elihu's doctrinal statement that God disregards improper things; not a direction. Shares wording with 34:12 but not its warning.
Prayer addressed to God ('Thy praises'); out of scope. Shares wording with Psalm 72:28 only.
Lament later cited as fulfilled at John 19:24; it directs no one. AUD-47-19-23 notes the citation without linking it.
Imprecatory prayer addressed to God; out of scope. Shares 'according to their works' with Romans 2:6 only.

context: Earlier form of the same saying: the sinner watches the righteous and gnashes his teeth, but the Lord laughs at him.
reason: Repeats the 36:32–33 saying (sinner watches the righteous; the Lord intervenes), linked as 36:25–26 is to 36:21; cf. N:GAP-21-36-9.
Narrative opening of the theophany; God's summons is recorded in direct speech at 49:5 and 49:7. Shares only a phrase with 112:3.

context: Psalm 52 repeats Psalm 13's closing verse; the Saints text renders it indicative ('Jacob will exult').
reason: Doublet of Psalm 13:7; the record's own note directs linking 52:7 as Additional Scripture, though the Saints text there is indicative.
Prayer addressed to God ('Attend to me and hear me'); out of scope. Shares only 'grieved' and 'troubled' with Micah 6:3.
First occurrence of the refrain recorded at 61:6–8, as the record's note says; same psalm and speaker. 61:2 included to keep the refrain whole.
Prayer-wish echoing the priestly blessing's words; it does not recall or repeat the command to bless (C0827).
Lament addressed to God about boasting sinners; out of scope. Shares wording with Psalm 74:6 only.
Doctrinal ground ('For the Lord will not reject') of the recorded beatitude 93:12–13, not a direction; shares doctrine with Lamentations 3:31 only.
Psalm statement Jesus cites in the tenants parable; doctrine, not a direction. AUD-44-21-33 notes the citation without linking the psalm.
Prayer addressed to God ('teach me Thine ordinances'); out of scope. The petition at 118:12 is covered only as part of a recorded stanza.
Prayer addressed to God ('Help me, and I will be saved'); out of scope. Shares meditation wording with 118:16 only.
David's vow about his own conduct; a self-commitment, not a direction. Shares sleep imagery with Proverbs 6:4 only.
